race_name: L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera

top_categories.workout_context: L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera's mountain passes forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 69 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
7,021ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
69 miles on mountain passes burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
101ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Base fitness for L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera. Train it until it feels boring.
7,021ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on mountain passes. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
Smooth pedaling at 69 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.

race_overlay.heat: July in Peshtera, Bulgaria can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera’s 69 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at L'Étape Bulgaria by Tour de France - Peshtera demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride mountain passes at race-day cadence weekly. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Test tires and pressure in comparable conditions before race week rather than guessing from a generic time-loss claim.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and VO2max to prepare you for 69 miles of mountain passes in Peshtera, Bulgaria.
